raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

This PR is powered by [KDA](https://github.com/NVlabs/kda) team. `MuseSpark1xRouter` computes FP32 router logits on a side stream in every MoE layer, and the MoE waits for it. At one decode token cuBLAS runs this as a split-K GEMV plus a separate reduce kernel. In NVFP4 batch-1 decode on GB300 the main stream waits 146-152 us per step (of about 5.4 ms) for the router.

## Modifications

- `kernels/ops/gemm/muse_spark_router_gemv_cutedsl.py` (new): a CuTe DSL FP32 GEMV with one launch, no split-K workspace and a fixed reduction order, so results are deterministic and differ from cuBLAS only by FP32 summation order
- `router_gemv_cute_eligible` admits FP32 inputs on SM10x GPUs with aligned rows. Muse Spark enables TF32, under which cuBLAS already runs multi-row logits as a TF32 GEMM, so only the one-token decode call moves
- `srt/models/muse_spark.py`: `MuseSpark1xRouter.forward` calls the kernel when eligible and keeps `F.linear` otherwise
- `kernels/ops/gemm/__init__.py`, `test_kernels_namespace.py`: register `gemm.muse_spark_router_gemv` in the kernel inventory
- `test_muse_spark_router_gemv_cutedsl.py` (new): FP64 reference with an FP32 error bound, 1-16 tokens, misaligned rows, other shapes, bitwise repeatability, side-stream CUDA-graph replay and the TF32 dispatch rule. Registered on H100 (fallback path) and B200 (CuTe path)

## Accuracy Tests

- 16,600 cases over 200 configurations stay within the FP32 error bound (largest error 0.5% of it); Compute Sanitizer is clean
- GSM8K (sgl-eval, 1319 questions, 8 runs per side): NVFP4 +0.27 pt (95% CI [-0.13, +0.69]), BF16 -0.08 pt ([-0.50, +0.34])

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel vs cuBLAS on GB300 at one token (hidden 8192, 256 experts), two jobs:

| Weight | cuBLAS | CuTe DSL | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cold (HBM) | 6.24 us | 4.19 us | 1.49x / 1.50x |
| warm | 4.35 us | 2.14 us | 2.03x / 2.03x |

Model, cookbook GB300 High Throughput recipe, decode-C1 mean ITL, two pairs per format:

| Format | Pair 1 | Pair 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NVFP4 (1x GB300, TP4/EP4) | 1.017x | 1.007x |
| BF16 (2x GB300, TP8/EP8) | 1.030x | 1.031x |

- No repeatable regression above 2% at any serving point in either format
- The Low Latency (DFlash) recipe never calls the kernel: its verify steps route several tokens per request (0 launches in the rank-0 profiles)
- Measured before [#45112](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45112) moved the kernel to `ops/gemm/`; on current main the tests pass on GB300, and GSM8K with the other Muse Spark changes applied shows no loss (NVFP4 over five pairs +0.00 pt, BF16 +0.19 pt)

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not applicable.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -0,0 +1,203 @@
+"""CuTe DSL skinny FP32 router GEMV for MuseSpark decode: ``logits[T, E] = x[T, K] @ w[E, K]^T``.
+
+cuBLAS runs this as a split-K GEMV plus a separate reduction kernel on the router side
+stream, which then finishes after the main-stream expert input and stalls the MoE.
+Here one CTA owns one (T = 1) or two weight rows over the whole K range: each thread
+issues all of its 16-byte weight loads before the first FMA, streams the T token rows
+of x against them, and the partial sums are reduced by a butterfly shuffle within each
+warp and then across warps in a fixed order through shared memory. There is no split-K
+workspace or second launch, and the summation order is fixed, so results are
+deterministic (they differ from cuBLAS only by FP32 summation order).
+"""
+
+from functools import cache
+from typing import Optional
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import is_arch_support_pdl
+
+MAX_TOKENS = 8
+# GB300 sweep (cold weight, side stream): 512 threads; one expert per CTA at T = 1
+# (more CTAs in flight), two above (x rows are re-read from L2 once per CTA).
+_THREADS = 512
+_VEC = 4  # FP32 elements per 16-byte load
+
+
+def _experts_per_cta(tokens: int) -> int:
+    return 1 if tokens == 1 else 2
+
+
+@cache
+def _is_sm100_family(device_index: int) -> bool:
+    return torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device_index)[0] == 10
+
+
+def router_gemv_cute_eligible(x: torch.Tensor, w: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
+    """FP32 decode-sized inputs with 16-byte aligned rows on SM100-family GPUs.
+
+    With TF32 matmuls allowed (``float32_matmul_precision != "highest"``, as the
+    server sets for MuseSpark) cuBLAS runs multi-row logits as a TF32 GEMM, so
+    only the single-row call, which cuBLAS still runs as an FP32 GEMV, moves here.
+    """
+    return (
+        x.is_cuda
+        and x.dtype == torch.float32
+        and w.dtype == torch.float32
+        and x.dim() == 2
+        and w.dim() == 2
+        and 1 <= x.shape[0] <= MAX_TOKENS
+        and (x.shape[0] == 1 or torch.get_float32_matmul_precision() == "highest")
+        and x.shape[1] == w.shape[1]
+        and x.device == w.device
+        and x.stride(1) == 1
+        and x.stride(0) % _VEC == 0
+        and x.data_ptr() % 16 == 0
+        and w.is_contiguous()
+        and w.data_ptr() % 16 == 0
+        and w.shape[1] % (_THREADS * _VEC) == 0
+        and w.shape[0] % 2 == 0
+        and _is_sm100_family(x.device.index)
+    )
+
+
+def router_gemv_cute(
+    x: torch.Tensor, w: torch.Tensor, use_pdl: Optional[bool] = None
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``x @ w.T`` as a contiguous FP32 ``[T, E]`` tensor."""
+    if use_pdl is None:
+        use_pdl = is_arch_support_pdl()
+    out = torch.empty(x.shape[0], w.shape[0], dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
+    _compile(x.shape[0], w.shape[1], bool(use_pdl))(x, w, out)
+    return out
+
+
+@cache
+def _compile(tokens, hidden, use_pdl):
+    import cutlass
+    import cutlass.cute as cute
+
+    kernel = _kernel_type()(tokens, hidden, use_pdl)
+    x = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(
+        cutlass.Float32,
+        (tokens, hidden),
+        (cute.sym_int64(divisibility=_VEC), 1),
+        assumed_align=16,
+    )
+    w = cute.runtime.make_fake_compact_tensor(
+        cutlass.Float32,
+        (cute.sym_int(), hidden),
+        stride_order=(1, 0),
+        assumed_align=16,
+    )
+    out = cute.runtime.make_fake_compact_tensor(
+        cutlass.Float32, (tokens, cute.sym_int()), stride_order=(1, 0), assumed_align=4
+    )
+    return cute.compile(
+        kernel,
+        x,
+        w,
+        out,
+        cute.runtime.make_fake_stream(use_tvm_ffi_env_stream=True),
+        options="--enable-tvm-ffi",
+    )
+
+
+@cache
+def _kernel_type():
+    import cutlass
+    import cutlass.cute as cute
+    from cutlass import Float32
+
+    class RouterGemv:
+        def __init__(self, tokens, hidden, use_pdl):
+            self.tokens = tokens
+            self.experts = _experts_per_cta(tokens)
+            self.warps = _THREADS // 32
+            self.iters = hidden // (_THREADS * _VEC)
+            self.outputs = tokens * self.experts
+            self.use_pdl = use_pdl
+
+        @cute.jit
+        def __call__(self, mX: cute.Tensor, mW: cute.Tensor, mOut: cute.Tensor, stream):
+            red = cute.make_layout((self.warps, self.outputs))
+            self.kernel(mX, mW, mOut).launch(
+                grid=[mW.shape[0] // self.experts, 1, 1],
+                block=[_THREADS, 1, 1],
+                smem=cute.size_in_bytes(Float32, red),
+                stream=stream,
+                use_pdl=self.use_pdl,
+            )
+
+        @cute.kernel
+        def kernel(self, mX: cute.Tensor, mW: cute.Tensor, mOut: cute.Tensor):
+            tidx, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()
+            bidx, _, _ = cute.arch.block_idx()
+            warp = tidx // 32
+            lane = tidx % 32
+            n0 = bidx * self.experts
+            if cutlass.const_expr(self.use_pdl):
+                cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+                cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()
+            atom = cute.make_copy_atom(
+                cute.nvgpu.CopyUniversalOp(), Float32, num_bits_per_copy=128
+            )
+            # Partition a complete CTA tile so the copy carries an explicit
+            # contiguous four-value layout. A per-thread local_tile(1, 4)
+            # loses vectorization and lowers to four strided scalar loads.
+            copy_slice = cute.make_tiled_copy(
+                atom,
+                cute.make_layout(
+                    ((_THREADS, 1), (_VEC, 1)),
+                    stride=((_VEC, 1), (1, _THREADS * _VEC)),
+                ),
+                (1, _THREADS * _VEC),
+            ).get_slice(tidx)
+            # Every weight load of this thread goes out before the first FMA.
+            ws = []
+            for e in cutlass.range_constexpr(self.experts):
+                for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(self.iters):
+                    src = copy_slice.partition_S(
+                        cute.local_tile(mW, (1, _THREADS * _VEC), (n0 + e, i))
+                    )
+                    frag = cute.make_fragment_like(src)
+                    cute.copy(atom, src, frag)
+                    ws.append(frag)
+            acc = []  # index t * experts + e
+            for t in cutlass.range_constexpr(self.tokens):
+                xs = []
+                for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(self.iters):
+                    src = copy_slice.partition_S(
+                        cute.local_tile(mX, (1, _THREADS * _VEC), (t, i))
+                    )
+                    frag = cute.make_fragment_like(src)
+                    cute.copy(atom, src, frag)
+                    xs.append(frag)
+                for e in cutlass.range_constexpr(self.experts):
+                    s = Float32(0.0)
+                    for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(self.iters):
+                        for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(_VEC):
+                            s = s + xs[i][j] * ws[e * self.iters + i][j]
+                    acc.append(s)
+            for v in cutlass.range_constexpr(self.outputs):
+                for step in cutlass.range_constexpr(5):
+                    acc[v] = acc[v] + cute.arch.shuffle_sync_bfly(
+                        acc[v], offset=1 << step
+                    )
+            smem = cutlass.utils.SmemAllocator()
+            red = smem.allocate_tensor(
+                Float32, cute.make_layout((self.warps, self.outputs)), 16
+            )
+            if lane == 0:
+                for v in cutlass.range_constexpr(self.outputs):
+                    red[warp, v] = acc[v]
+            cute.arch.sync_threads()
+            # Fixed cross-warp order keeps the result deterministic.
+            if tidx < self.outputs:
+                total = red[0, tidx]
+                for wi in cutlass.range_constexpr(1, self.warps):
+                    total = total + red[wi, tidx]
+                t = tidx // self.experts
+                mOut[t, n0 + tidx - t * self.experts] = total
+
+    return RouterGemv

@@ -30,6 +30,10 @@
 from sglang.kernels.ops.gemm.muse_spark_router_gemm import (
     MAX_TOKENS as ROUTER_GEMM_MAX_TOKENS,
 )
+from sglang.kernels.ops.gemm.muse_spark_router_gemv_cutedsl import (
+    router_gemv_cute,
+    router_gemv_cute_eligible,
+)
 from sglang.kernels.ops.layernorm.muse_spark_norm_gate import FusedRMSNormGate
 from sglang.kernels.ops.layernorm.muse_spark_norm_residual import (
     FusedPostNormResidualPreNorm,
@@ -231,6 +235,9 @@ def forward_split2(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
         return acc

+        # Decode-sized FP32 logits: one CuTe GEMV instead of cuBLAS split-K + reduce.
+        if router_gemv_cute_eligible(hidden_states, self.weight):
+            return router_gemv_cute(hidden_states, self.weight)
         return F.linear(hidden_states, self.weight)

@@ -0,0 +1,132 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Muse Spark FP32 router logits (MuseSpark1xRouter): FP64 semantics, dispatch and graph state.
+
+Any-order FP32 dot products satisfy |fl(s) - s| <= gamma_K * sum_k |x_k w_k| plus an
+underflow term; small-integer inputs keep every partial sum exact, so any summation
+order must return the exact logits there. Decode-sized (T <= 8) FP32 inputs with
+16-byte aligned rows run the CuTe DSL GEMV on SM100-family GPUs (only T = 1 when TF32
+matmuls are allowed); everything else runs F.linear. Results are bitwise repeatable,
+including side-stream CUDA-graph replay.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.gemm.muse_spark_router_gemv_cutedsl import (
+    MAX_TOKENS,
+    router_gemv_cute_eligible,
+)
+from sglang.srt.models.muse_spark import MuseSpark1xRouter
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA required")
+U = 2.0**-24
+
+
+def _router(w):
+    router = MuseSpark1xRouter(w.shape[1], w.shape[0], dtype=torch.float32).cuda()
+    router.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(w, requires_grad=False)
+    return router
+
+
+def _inputs(tokens, hidden, experts, dist, pad=0, seed=0):
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda")
+    g.manual_seed(seed)
+    if dist == "integer":
+        x = torch.randint(
+            -8, 9, (tokens, hidden + pad), generator=g, device="cuda"
+        ).float()
+        w = torch.randint(-8, 9, (experts, hidden), generator=g, device="cuda").float()
+    else:
+        x = torch.randn(tokens, hidden + pad, generator=g, device="cuda")
+        w = torch.randn(experts, hidden, generator=g, device="cuda") / hidden**0.5
+        if dist == "wide":
+            x = x * torch.exp2(
+                torch.randint(-30, 31, x.shape, generator=g, device="cuda").float()
+            )
+    return x[:, :hidden], w
+
+
+def _check(out, x, w, exact):
+    assert out.shape == (x.shape[0], w.shape[0]) and out.dtype == torch.float32
+    assert out.stride() == (w.shape[0], 1)
+    xd, wd = x.double(), w.double()
+    ref = xd @ wd.t()
+    k = x.shape[1]
+    bound = k * U / (1 - k * U) * (xd.abs() @ wd.abs().t()) + (2 * k + 1) * 2.0**-150
+    err = (out.double() - ref).abs()
+    if exact:
+        assert torch.equal(out.double(), ref)
+    else:
+        assert bool((err <= bound).all()), float((err / bound).max())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tokens", [1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dist", ["normal", "wide", "integer"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("pad", [0, 4, 3])
+def test_router_logits_semantics(tokens, dist, pad):
+    x, w = _inputs(tokens, 8192, 256, dist, pad, seed=tokens * 31 + pad)
+    router = _router(w)
+    before = (x.clone(), w.clone())
+    eligible = router_gemv_cute_eligible(x, w)
+    sm100 = torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] == 10
+    assert torch.get_float32_matmul_precision() == "highest"
+    assert eligible == (sm100 and tokens <= MAX_TOKENS and pad % 4 == 0)
+    out = router(x)
+    out2 = router(x)
+    _check(out, x, w, dist == "integer")
+    assert torch.equal(out.view(torch.int32), out2.view(torch.int32))

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tokens", [1, 8])
+def test_router_side_stream_graph_replay(tokens):
+    x, w = _inputs(tokens, 8192, 256, "normal", seed=tokens)
+    router = _router(w)
+    sources = [
+        _inputs(tokens, 8192, 256, "normal", seed=100 + i)[0].contiguous()
+        for i in range(3)
+    ]
+    expected = [router(s).clone() for s in sources]
+    src = sources[0].clone()
+    main = torch.cuda.current_stream()
+    capture, side = torch.cuda.Stream(), torch.cuda.Stream()
+    capture.wait_stream(main)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=capture):
+        x.copy_(src)
+        side.wait_stream(capture)
+        with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+            out = router(x)
+        capture.wait_stream(side)
+    for rep in range(30):
+        src.copy_(sources[rep % 3])
+        out.fill_(float("nan"))
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.equal(out.view(torch.int32), expected[rep % 3].view(torch.int32))
